title: High-risk AI systems
note: Annex III lists 8 areas of use. An AI system used in any of these is high-risk under Article 6(2), with limited exceptions in Article 6(3). Verify the latest text on EUR-Lex for any edge case.

categories.name: Biometrics
categories.scope: Remote biometric identification systems, biometric categorisation systems based on sensitive attributes, emotion recognition systems
examples: Voice-based emotion analysis in call centers
common_saas_features_in_scope: Voice analytics for customer support tone-scoring
Identity verification kiosks with biometric matching

categories.name: Critical infrastructure
categories.scope: Safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, water, gas, heating, electricity
examples: Predictive maintenance AI for power grid relays
common_saas_features_in_scope: SaaS that supplies algorithms or models directly to grid operators or municipal water companies

categories.name: Education and vocational training
categories.scope: Admissions decisions, assignment to programmes, evaluation of learning outcomes, assessment of appropriate level of education, monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour during tests
examples: Plagiarism detection that influences a final grade
common_saas_features_in_scope: EdTech SaaS that auto-scores essays or exams
Proctoring SaaS with attention or behaviour analytics
Course recommendation that determines programme assignment

categories.name: Employment, worker management, and access to self-employment
categories.scope: Recruitment or selection, decisions affecting terms of work, promotion, termination, allocation of tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits, monitoring and evaluating performance
examples: CV screening that filters or ranks candidates
Algorithmic task assignment for gig workers
Sentiment analysis on internal employee communications
common_saas_features_in_scope: HR SaaS with resume screening, candidate ranking, or interview scoring
Workforce management SaaS that allocates shifts or tasks via AI
Performance management SaaS that scores employees from data

categories.name: Access to and enjoyment of essential public and private services
categories.scope: Eligibility for public assistance benefits and services, creditworthiness evaluation or credit scoring (except detection of financial fraud), risk assessment and pricing for life and health insurance, dispatch or prioritisation of emergency services

categories.name: Law enforcement
categories.scope: Risk assessment of natural persons as potential victims or offenders, polygraph and similar tools, assessment of evidence reliability, predictive policing based on profiling, criminal analytics
common_saas_features_in_scope: B2G platforms supplying analytics to police or prosecutorial agencies

categories.name: Migration, asylum, and border control management
categories.scope: Polygraph and similar tools, risk assessments related to entry, examination of applications for asylum and visas, detection and recognition of natural persons at borders
common_saas_features_in_scope: Government-facing visa or asylum processing SaaS

categories.name: Administration of justice and democratic processes
categories.scope: AI systems intended to assist judicial authorities in researching and interpreting facts and law and in applying the law to a concrete set of facts, AI used for influencing the outcome of an election or voting behaviour
examples: Legal research AI used by judges
common_saas_features_in_scope: LegalTech SaaS sold to courts or tribunals

exception_article_6_3: An AI system referred to in Annex III is NOT high-risk if it does not pose a significant risk of harm to health, safety, or fundamental rights, including by not materially influencing the outcome of decision-making. Conditions in Article 6(3) include: AI performs a narrow procedural task, AI improves the result of a previously completed human activity, AI detects decision-making patterns or deviations without replacing the human assessment, AI performs a preparatory task. Profiling of natural persons is always considered high-risk.
obligations_if_high_risk: Transparency and provision of information to deployers (Article 13)
Registration in EU database (Article 49 and Article 71)
